<!--
PERFORMANCE REPORT BLOCK — the standard table + figures of a backtest.

How to use, in a post's index.qmd:

1. In an earlier chunk, define:
     returns    pd.DataFrame of daily SIMPLE returns, one column per series,
                the strategy first (e.g. ["Strategy", "VALE3"]).
                From log returns: returns = to_simple_returns(log_returns)
     benchmark  name of the benchmark column, or None
2. Where the report should appear, add this line (outside any chunk), with
   TWO braces on each side (written here with three, the escaped form, because
   Quarto expands shortcodes even inside comments and this file would include
   itself forever):
     {{{< include /_templates/_performance.qmd >}}}

The block brings its own imports. Its labels (tbl-performance, fig-perf-*) can
be cited in the text, e.g. "the drawdown (@fig-perf-drawdown) shows ...".
The captions are generic: to comment on a figure in its own words, skip the
block and call the plot functions directly in the post.
-->

```{python}
#| label: perf-setup
#| include: false
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from investigating.performance import (
    metrics_table,
    performance_metrics,
    plot_cumulative,
    plot_drawdown,
    plot_monthly_heatmap,
    plot_rolling_sharpe,
    plot_rolling_volatility,
)

perf_benchmark = globals().get("benchmark")
perf_strategy = next(c for c in returns.columns if c != perf_benchmark)
perf_metrics = performance_metrics(returns)
perf_period = f"{perf_metrics.attrs['start']:%b %Y} – {perf_metrics.attrs['end']:%b %Y}"
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-performance
#| tbl-cap: "Performance metrics over the common period. Daily simple returns, 252 sessions per year, risk-free rate of zero."
metrics_table(returns)
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-perf-cumulative
#| fig-cap: "Cumulative return, log scale: equal vertical distances are equal percentage moves."
plot_cumulative(returns, benchmark=perf_benchmark, log_scale=True)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-perf-drawdown
#| fig-cap: "Drawdown: the fall from the previous peak at each date. The shaded area is the strategy."
plot_drawdown(returns, benchmark=perf_benchmark)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-perf-monthly
#| fig-cap: "Monthly returns of the strategy. The year column has its own color scale."
plot_monthly_heatmap(returns[perf_strategy])
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-perf-rolling
#| fig-cap: "Six-month rolling Sharpe ratio (top) and annualized volatility (bottom)."
#| fig-height: 6
fig, (ax_top, ax_bottom) = plt.subplots(2, 1, sharex=True, figsize=(9, 6), layout="constrained")
plot_rolling_sharpe(returns, benchmark=perf_benchmark, ax=ax_top)
plot_rolling_volatility(returns, benchmark=perf_benchmark, ax=ax_bottom, legend=False)
plt.show()
```
